chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from some of his companions who said:

Al-Abrash al-Kalbi complained to Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) that no child was being born to him. So he said to him (AS): 'Teach me something.' He (AS) said: 'Seek forgiveness of God during every day or every night one hundred times.'
For God says: 'Ask forgiveness of your Lord, surely He is the Most Forgiving — up to His words: And He will aid you with wealth and sons.'

key_terms.اسْتَغْفِرِ اللَّهَ: Seek forgiveness from God — a supplicatory practice (istighfar) involving sincere repentance and asking God's pardon
key_terms.غَفَّاراً: Most Forgiving — intensive form indicating God's abundant and repeated forgiveness
key_terms.مِائَةَ مَرَّةٍ: One hundred times — a specific prescribed number for the practice
key_terms.وَيُمْدِدْكُمْ بِأَمْوَالٍ وَبَنِينَ: And He will aid you with wealth and sons — the Quranic promise of material and progeny blessings as a result of istighfar

ai.seo_question: What supplication did Imam al-Baqir prescribe for childlessness?
ai.summary: Al-Abrash al-Kalbi, a companion, sought the counsel of Imam Muhammad al-Baqir (AS) because he had no children. The Imam prescribed seeking God's forgiveness (istighfar) one hundred times daily, citing the Quranic promise in Surah Nuh (71:10-12) that God responds to sincere forgiveness-seeking with blessings including offspring and wealth. This hadith presents istighfar as a spiritual remedy for infertility, connecting it directly to the Quranic promise made through Prophet Nuh to his people.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from one of his companions who said,

‘Al-Abrash Al-Kalby complained to Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> that there is no child for him. So he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘Teach me something (to have a son)’. He<sup>asws</sup> said: ‘Seek Forgiveness of Allah<sup>azwj</sup> during every day, or during every night, one hundred times, for Allah<sup>azwj</sup> is Saying
[71:10] So I said, Ask forgiveness of your Lord, surely He is the most Forgiving – up to Hisazwj Words [71:12] And Help you with wealth and sons’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from certain persons of his people who has said the following: “Once al-Abrash al-Kalbiy complained before abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and said that he did not have any child and asked him (the Imam) to teach him something.
He (the Imam) said, say, ‘I ask forgiveness from Allah, my Lord and return to Him in repentance’ one hundred times every day and every night,
because Allah says, ‘Ask forgiveness from your Lord; He is forgiving. ... He helps you by means of your wealth and sons.’” [71:10]
